note: Editable starting points for SubmitDefenseValidationRequest@1. Not a registry: the service never resolves anything from here during a run. Each file is a complete payload and can be submitted directly.

examples.title: Direct proof, candidate blocks, benign preserved
examples.narrative: Dev-equivalent WAF, direct root-cause attack baseline reaches the vulnerable path, the candidate blocks it, benign suite preserved.

examples.title: Indirect discriminator proof
examples.narrative: Discriminator-backed attack cases blocked and benign preserved; the indirect proof path is recorded as an explicit limitation.

examples.title: Required attack still reaches the target
examples.narrative: An earlier candidate revision covers only one signature; the remaining required attacks reach the protected target while benign traffic is preserved.

examples.title: Benign regression governs over attack failure
examples.narrative: An over-broad candidate blocks legitimate requests. A required attack also slips through; both findings are retained and `unsafe` governs.

examples.title: Context engine version outside profile
examples.narrative: The context runs an engine major version the approved profile does not support, so no candidate judgment is made.

examples.title: Context configuration drift
examples.narrative: The live control reports a configuration fingerprint that differs from the supplied context descriptor.

examples.title: Generic rejection with no attribution
examples.narrative: The context declares control-decision observability but the control emits only a generic rejection, so blocking cannot be attributed to the candidate.

examples.title: Unsupported suite modality
examples.narrative: A stateful browser journey is submitted against a stateless-HTTP profile; the request is valid but outside configured coverage.

examples.title: Unsupported proof path
examples.narrative: An indirect suite is submitted against a direct-only profile.

examples.title: Candidate application fails, state unknown
examples.narrative: The rule commit times out without acknowledgement; actual control state cannot be established, so no domain result can be emitted.

examples.title: Same block with and without the candidate
examples.narrative: An unrelated legacy edge filter blocks the attack traffic in both trials with no attribution, so blocking is not candidate-attributable.

examples.title: Production context denied at the edge
examples.narrative: A payload naming a production control context is rejected before any run is created; this is an authorization boundary, not a domain outcome.
